subject: Literature
title: Elizabethan Theatre Culture
description: A quick win: understand Elizabethan Theatre Culture.

hook.text: Elizabethan theatres were rowdy, smelly, and dangerous, more like a football match than a quiet concert hall.

buildup.text: Groundlings stood in the open pit, eating hazelnuts and heckling actors while nobles sat in covered galleries.

discovery.text: All female roles were played by boys, since women were forbidden from performing on the English stage.

twist.text: Plays competed with bear-baiting arenas next door, so playwrights had to be thrilling to survive financially.

climax.text: This rough, competitive environment forced Shakespeare to write plays that gripped every class of audience.

punchline.text: Shakespeare's rival was a bear pit next door.

quiz.question: Why were Elizabethan plays so dramatic and engaging?
options: Theatres competed with bear-baiting arenas for the same audiences
Actors were paid based on applause volume
